correctness.rationale: Exact orthonormal-basis action gives a weighted partial permutation with source/destination sets pairwise distinct. Uniform gamma-ratio asymptotics yield the exact positive 1/k defect coefficient, which gives singular-value and logarithmic limits. For unequal degrees, integer-multiplication graph has no cycles and has arbitrarily long disjoint paths; endpoint approximate kernels and unit-circle Weyl vectors establish the Fredholm disk, while Neumann inversion excludes the exterior. Boundedly many low-index exceptional weights per forward orbit prove the full positive-degree spectral-radius bound. The distinct-degree claim does not include self-products, whose unweighted spectral formulas were studied previously in 2015. Exact finite arithmetic corroborates matrix and coefficient identities but is not used in infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The recently studied natural product C_{z^m} C_{z^n}^* is noncompact, so the exact Fredholm spectrum and the optimal compact correction to its partial-permutation limit are substantive operator invariants. Distinct-degree monomial cross-products exhibit an exact positive-radius Fredholm disk with a simple outlying constant eigenvalue; the universal 1/k correction additionally gives a meaningful weak-trace-class endpoint for every classical radial weighted Bergman space.
